newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: G10 NOT CONCERNED ABOUT EXCHANGE RATES - TIETMEYER.
newsitem.headline: G10 NOT CONCERNED ABOUT EXCHANGE RATES - TIETMEYER.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said Group of 10 (G10) central bank governors saw no reason to be concerned about currency exchange rates within Europe or between Europe and the U.S. dollar.
Tietmeyer said the monthly meeting of G10 central bank governors at the Bank for International Settlements had discussed exchange rates between their countries.
"I haven't heard any concern about the present situation, at least as far as relationship inside Europe and between the dollar and the European area is concerned," Tietmeyer told reporters.
Tietmeyer said the latest indicators and forecasts from Group of 10 (G10) countries showed economic growth within the group was strengthening and would accelerate modestly this year and in 1998.
But Tietmeyer also said unemployment remained the most difficult part of the economic situation in continental Europe.

"The latest forecasts continue to suggest a modest acceleration of real growth this year as far as the G10 group is concerned," Tietmeyer told reporters. "It is expected that this acceleration will be sustained in 1998," he added.
Tietmeyer said inflation was under control in practially all of the Group of 10 countries, and monetary policy in these countries was also appropriate.
He added that inflation was never dead and could resurface, so monetary policy had to remain vigilant.
He said this was the case "in some countries more than in others, because of different growth rates."
He made his comments to reporters after the G10 meeting at the Bank for International Settlements (BIS).
"All in all, inflation seems to be in practically all countries under control, and monetary policy seems to be in most countries appropriate," Tietmeyer said.
He said that the Group of 10 discussed the situation on Japanese financial markets, but he declined to specify whether they drew any conclusions.
Tietmeyer also said the group of 10 central banks had "no intention" for the time being to sell any gold.
